chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:

It is not that Allāh may keep the door of gratitude open for a servant and close the door of plenty upon him, or to open the door of prayer to a servant and close the door of acceptance upon him, or to open the door of repentance for a servant and close the door of forgiveness upon him.
ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between gratitude, prayer, and repentance according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: In this narration from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) elucidates the principle of divine reciprocity (muqabala), emphasizing that God’s opening of a 'door' to an act of worship inherently guarantees the opening of the corresponding door to its reward. This reflects the Shia scholarly understanding of God’s consistency (istiqara) in His covenant, where gratitude (shukr) leads to increase (ziyada), supplication (dua) leads to acceptance (ijaba), and repentance (tawba) leads to forgiveness (maghfira). The hadith serves as a theological assurance that divine generosity is not arbitrary but follows a precise, promised logic rooted in His mercy.
